inputs.root_cause: SAL-NRRD-OBL-00F18A8DA59864CD and SAL-NRRD-OBL-38F3D4743DF2B0F9 (both NRRD-PHYSICALMETA-001) require modeling 'sample units' (NRRD0004+, distinct from per-axis units/space units/thicknesses). No sample_units accessor existed anywhere in the model, and the field was not version-gated at all, confirmed by grepping document.py directly.
inputs.acceptance_evidence: NrrdDocument.sample_units now reads either the 'sample units' or 'sampleunits' header spelling (both spec-legal per the pinned source) and returns a plain unquoted string, correctly distinct from the per-axis quoted units/labels syntax. version_requirements() now gates it at NRRD0004+. 9 new tests prove both spellings, absence, unquoted-plain-text parsing, round-trip, distinctness from axis units, and write-time version-gate refusal.
inputs.regression_tier: full nrrd package suite (tests/python/nrrd) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. Grepped document.py for 'sample units'/'sample_units' -- zero hits, confirming the field is genuinely unmodeled, not a stale citation.

2. Read the pinned spec source directly (.local/format-contracts/acquired/nrrd/src-nrrd-001.bin, SRC-NRRD-001): found the field's exact definition -- 'sample units: <string>' / 'sampleunits: <string>', 'Always optional. This provides a way of storing the units of measurement associated with the scalar values stored in the array itself... Note that these units describe the individual scalar values, and not some non-scalar value stored along an axis of the array.' Also confirmed the worked example ('sample units: PPM') is unquoted plain text, correcting the obligation's own paraphrase ('a single quoted unit') against the actual spec wording before writing any code.

3. Confirmed via the spec's own field-list groupings that 'sample units' is a 'Basic field specification' (single, whole-document value) distinct from 'units' (a 'Per-axis field specification', quote-delimited per-axis list) -- the two are structurally different fields, not aliases of each other.

4. Added NrrdDocument.sample_units (reading either spelling via header.get() fallback chaining, matching the established line-skip/byte-skip alias pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase) and a version_requirements() entry gating it at NRRD0004+, mirroring the existing thicknesses gate exactly.

5. Verified interactively before writing any test: both field-name spellings project correctly, absence returns None, a round trip through dumps()/loads() preserves the value (writer.py's existing generic sorted-header-field loop already handles this field with no writer changes needed), and dumps(profile='NRRD0003') correctly refuses a document declaring sample units -- all 6 scenarios correct on the first attempt.

6. Caught and fixed a self-inflicted test-fixture bug before it reached a real test failure count: the first draft of a test file's _header() helper produced a spurious extra blank-line-terminator newline when the optional 'extra' field was empty, corrupting the payload boundary (confirmed via the actual NrrdParseError message: 'expected 2 bytes, got 3') -- fixed the helper to only emit the extra field line when non-empty, re-ran, all tests passed.

7. Wrote 9 new tests (7 in a new file, 2 extending the existing version-selection test file's established pattern). Ran ruff (clean) and the full nrrd suite (540 passed, was 531, +9) before writing any evidence claim. Ran the full 6-format regression (3079 passed, was 3070, +9; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/pytest tests/python/ipynb tests/python/ora tests/python/nrrd tests/python/xliff tests/python/safetensors tests/python/ubl -q -- 3079 passed, 2 skipped, 4 preexisting unrelated safetensors interop failures, was 3070 passed
